extracted.intended_audience: federal regulators, energy policymakers, electric cooperative leaders and stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes NRECA's comments and policy recommendations to DOE and FERC about serving rapidly growing large loads (e.g., data centers), focusing on regulatory alignment, reliability, cost allocation, and support for cooperatives. Useful for drafting or evaluating notice-and-comment filings on large-load interconnection and related federal initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-of-government approach
rubrics_metrics.description: “We urge a whole-of-government approach to ensure the federal regulations, policies and incentives are aligned to enable cooperatives and other utilities to make the investments needed to not only serve large loads... but to also protect affordability and reliability on the grid for all Americans.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy makers should coordinate across federal agencies so regulations, policies, and incentives are consistent and supportive of utilities' ability to invest to serve large loads while safeguarding affordability and reliability. This is presented as a central organizing principle for federal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support DOE Speed-to-Power Initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: NRECA provided input on the DOE’s Speed-to-Power Initiative, which aims to accelerate the addition of electricity resources to serve large energy users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal initiatives that accelerate resource additions for large users (e.g., Speed-to-Power) should be engaged with and shaped to ensure co-ops can access and benefit from efforts to bring new capacity online quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address stranded investment risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-ops are at risk of stranded investments if large loads do not come to fruition or fail to use as much electricity as expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should explicitly mitigate the financial risk that utilities (especially co-ops) face from investments made to serve prospective large loads that later do not materialize or underutilize capacity. Guidance includes adjusting funding, incentives, or cost-allocation mechanisms to reduce exposure to stranded assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain co-op access to federal tax incentives and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: NRECA called for policies that address those risks and to maintain co-op access to federal tax incentives and government funding for infrastructure projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cooperative utilities remain eligible for federal tax incentives and infrastructure funding programs so they can finance required transmission and generation investments to serve large loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC policies must support bulk power system reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Such policies must support bulk power system reliability and respect the importance of local control to electric co-ops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When FERC standardizes policies for connecting large loads, the primary metric must be bulk power reliability; proposed rules should be evaluated on whether they preserve system reliability while enabling interconnections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect local/state control and allow regional flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NRECA asked FERC not to intrude on state and local authority over retail electric sales to large loads. If FERC seeks new authority there, it should allow for regional flexibility on how to serve those customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory changes should avoid preempting state/local control over retail sales. If federal authority is expanded, rules should permit regional approaches that reflect local conditions and co-op governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large loads should pay their own way
rubrics_metrics.description: The association also said large loads should “pay their own way” when connecting to the interstate transmission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost-allocation policies should require the interconnecting large load to bear the costs of system upgrades attributable to its connection rather than distributing those costs broadly to other customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not saddle other transmission customers with stranded costs
rubrics_metrics.description: “Other transmission customers should not bear stranded transmission costs for upgrades made to accommodate the interconnection of a large load that fails to materialize, does not operate as anticipated, or ceases operation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory frameworks should prevent allocation of costs for upgrades made for a specific large-load interconnection to be socialized across unrelated customers if the project underperforms, fails to materialize, or ceases operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize co-ops' role and rural advantages in serving data centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments highlighted how co-ops are “at the heart of data center development,” often serving rural areas with large tracts of land that can accommodate those facilities and offering essential electric, water and fiber network infrastructure at much lower costs than suburban providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy design should account for the practical advantages and constraints of cooperatives—including land availability and bundled infrastructure offerings—when planning for large-load development and interconnection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address permitting, planning, and supply-chain challenges for new generation/transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Building new generation and transmission to meet that demand is difficult, with co-ops facing a host of permitting, planning and supply chain challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective policy must tackle non-cost barriers (permitting timelines, planning coordination, supply chain constraints) that delay or raise the cost of building generation and transmission needed to serve large loads.
